title: A unified computational framework for single-cell data integration with optimal transport

nodes.text: uniPort is a unified single-cell data integration framework that combines a coupled variational autoencoder (coupled-VAE) with minibatch unbalanced optimal transport (Minibatch-UOT) to jointly embed heterogeneous single-cell multi-omics datasets into a shared latent space.
nodes.evidence: uniPort, a unified single-cell data integration framework that combines a coupled variational autoencoder (coupled-VAE) and minibatch unbalanced optimal transport (Minibatch-UOT)

nodes.text: uniPort uses a dataset-free encoder over highly variable common genes plus dataset-specific decoders (with dataset-specific batch normalization, DSBN) to leverage both common and dataset-specific genes, handling cross-dataset heterogeneity.
nodes.evidence: It leverages both highly variable common and dataset-specific genes for integration to handle the heterogeneity across datasets

nodes.text: Unlike linear methods such as Seurat (CCA), LIGER/DC3 (NMF), and Harmony, which cannot handle nonlinear deformations and only use common genes, uniPort captures nonlinear deformations and exploits dataset-specific genes.
nodes.evidence: these methods rely on linear operation, thus lacking the ability to handle nonlinear deformations across cellular modalities ... they only leverage filtered common genes, while ignoring the importance of dataset-specific genes

nodes.text: To the authors' knowledge, no prior method unifies integration of single-cell multi-omics together with spatially resolved transcriptomic data; uniPort addresses this gap.
nodes.evidence: to the best of our knowledge, no method has been developed for a unified integration of single-cell multi-omics as well as spatially resolved transcriptomic data

nodes.text: The Minibatch-UOT loss feeds gradients back to the encoder for better alignment, the minibatch strategy makes OT scalable to large datasets, and the unbalanced formulation suits heterogeneous data integration.
nodes.evidence: the minibatch strategy substantially improves the computational efficiency of OT, making it scalable to large datasets, and the unbalanced OT makes it more suitable for heterogeneous data integration

nodes.text: uniPort can deconvolute heterogeneous spatial transcriptomic data using the optimal transport plan directly, rather than relying on latent-space embedding for label transfer.
nodes.evidence: uniPort provides a flexible label transfer framework to deconvolute heterogeneous spatial transcriptomic data using an optimal transport plan, instead of embedding latent space

nodes.text: On paired PBMC scATAC/scRNA data, uniPort achieved the highest Silhouette coefficient (0.64), comparable overall to GLUE; GLUE had better FOSCTTM and Batch Entropy while uniPort led on Silhouette.
nodes.evidence: uniPort achieved the highest Silhouette coefficient of 0.64, while GLUE had the second highest Silhouette coefficient of 0.621

nodes.text: On unpaired mouse spleen scATAC/scRNA, uniPort achieved the highest Silhouette coefficient (0.709), slightly above scMC, Harmony, and Seurat.
nodes.evidence: uniPort achieved the highest Silhouette coefficient of 0.709, slightly higher than scMC (0.704), Harmony (0.704), and Seurat (0.699)

nodes.text: In unbalanced matching tasks (cell types removed from one modality), only uniPort and Seurat achieved stable performance across all three cases, with uniPort most robust under heterogeneity.
nodes.evidence: only uniPort and Seurat achieved stable performance in all three cases ... uniPort is more robust than the other methods when heterogeneity is presented

nodes.text: On MERFISH and scRNA integration, uniPort achieved the highest Silhouette coefficient (0.706) and total ARI/NMI/F1 score (2.404), and correctly identified ependymal cells as a MERFISH-specific cell type.
nodes.evidence: uniPort outperformed other methods with the highest Silhouette coefficient of 0.706 and the highest total score of 2.404

nodes.text: For gene imputation of held-out MERFISH genes from scRNA, uniPort significantly outperformed gimVI and Tangram, with the highest median/average Spearman and Pearson correlations (e.g., mSCC 0.259).
nodes.evidence: uniPort provided a significant improvement over the two compared methods on the MERFISH dataset ... demonstrated the highest mSCC (0.259), aSCC (0.26), mPCC (0.249)

nodes.text: Once the coupled-VAE is trained, it functions as a reference atlas, allowing uniPort to impute both common and dataset-specific genes across datasets via shared common genes.
nodes.evidence: once the coupled-VAE is trained well, it can be regarded as a reference atlas, in turn allowing uniPort to impute both common and specific genes
